meta.title: Diisocyanates (REACH) training in Brussels | Wisy Safety
dii.lead: Since 24 August 2023, a product containing 0.1% or more of diisocyanates may only be used industrially or professionally by a person who has successfully completed training on their safe use. Wisy Safety offers this training.
dii.plate_r1: Successful training required before any industrial or professional use
dii.plate_r2: Concentration threshold by weight, diisocyanates individually or in combination
dii.plate_r3: Training is renewed at least every five years
dii.plate_r4: Mandatory statement on the packaging of the products concerned
dii.plate_src: Source: EUR-Lex, OJ L 252, 4.8.2020(new tab)
dii.f_scope_d: anyone who uses — or supervises the use of — products with 0.1% or more of diisocyanates, industrially or professionally
dii.f_renew_d: renewal at least every 5 years; successful completion documented by the employer or self-employed person
dii.card_note: The training level (general, intermediate or advanced) depends on your uses: specify them in your request.
dii.s1_intro: Commission Regulation (EU) 2020/1149 of 3 August 2020 added diisocyanates to Annex XVII of the REACH Regulation (entry 74). What it provides, point by point:
dii.s1_l1: Since 24 August 2023, diisocyanates — on their own, in another substance or in a mixture — may only be used industrially or professionally if their concentration is below 0.1% by weight, or if the employer or self-employed person ensures that the user has successfully completed training on their safe use before use (point 1).
dii.s1_l2: This covers employed and self-employed workers who handle these products, and also those who supervise these tasks (point 3).
dii.s1_l3: The training includes instructions for the control of dermal and inhalation exposure; it is delivered by an expert in occupational safety and health with competence acquired through relevant vocational training (point 4).
dii.s1_l4: It complies with the provisions set by the Member State in which the user works (point 6).
dii.s1_l5: The employer or self-employed person documents the successful completion of the training, which is renewed at least every five years (point 8).
dii.s1_l6: Since 24 February 2022, the supplier passes on this information and places the following statement on the packaging, in a visibly distinct manner (point 2):
dii.s1_label: “As from 24 August 2023 adequate training is required before industrial or professional use”
dii.s1_why: Why these rules? Diisocyanates are classified as respiratory and skin sensitisers, category 1. The dossier behind the restriction estimated more than 5,000 new cases of occupational disease per year attributable to diisocyanates in the Union (recitals 1 and 2 of the regulation).
dii.src_reg: Commission Regulation (EU) 2020/1149 of 3 August 2020 — OJ L 252, 4.8.2020 (EUR-Lex)
dii.s2_intro: Three questions, taken from the text of the regulation. Nothing is sent or stored.
dii.c_q1: Do you use — or supervise the use of — a product whose label or safety data sheet mentions diisocyanates?
dii.c_q2: Is the diisocyanate concentration 0.1% by weight or more?
dii.c_q2_hint: Hint: since 24 February 2022, the packaging of the products concerned must bear the statement “As from 24 August 2023 adequate training is required before industrial or professional use”.
dii.c_q3: Is it an industrial or professional use (and not a private use)?
dii.r_yes: This applies to you. Under Regulation (EU) 2020/1149, training on the safe use of diisocyanates must have been successfully completed before the product is used.
dii.r_unknown: To be checked. Look at the product label and safety data sheet, or ask your supplier: since 24 February 2022, they must pass on the information about this training requirement.
dii.r_nodiiso: This product is not covered by the restriction on diisocyanates. The general rules on chemical agents still apply: talk to your prevention adviser.
dii.r_below: Below 0.1% by weight, the restriction does not apply to this product (point 1 a). The general rules on chemical agents still apply.
dii.r_private: The restriction covers industrial and professional uses. For private use, follow the instructions on the label and the safety data sheet.
dii.c_disclaimer: General guidance based on the text of the regulation: it does not replace the analysis of your prevention adviser.
dii.s3_h2: Three training levels, depending on your uses
dii.s3_intro: The regulation sets minimum content for each level (points 4 and 5). Each level builds on the previous one.
dii.t_gen_c: Chemistry of diisocyanates, toxicity hazards, exposure, limit values, causes of sensitisation, personal hygiene, personal protective equipment, ventilation, cleaning and leakages, disposal of empty packaging.
dii.t_mid_u: Open mixtures at ambient temperature, spraying in a ventilated booth, roller or brush application, dipping and pouring, post-treatment of articles that are not fully cured, cleaning and waste.
dii.t_mid_c: General training + additional behaviour-based aspects, maintenance, management of change, evaluation of existing safety instructions.
dii.t_adv_u: Articles that are still warm, foundry work, maintenance and repair with access to equipment, warm or hot formulations (> 45 °C), spraying in open air or with limited ventilation, high-energy spraying.
dii.t_adv_c: General and intermediate training + spraying outside a booth, open handling of warm formulations, additional certifications required for the uses concerned.
dii.s3_note: For each level, the regulation provides for certification or documented proof of successful completion. The level covered by a Wisy Safety session is confirmed when you send your request.
dii.s4_h2: In Belgium: limit values specific to diisocyanates
dii.s4_intro: The Royal Decree of 25 May 2026, published in the Belgian Official Gazette on 3 June 2026, sets uniform occupational exposure limit values for all diisocyanates (transposing Directive (EU) 2024/869).
dii.s4_p: These values come on top of the employer's general obligation to assess the risks linked to chemical agents present at the workplace and to take the necessary preventive measures (Codex on well-being at work, Book VI, Title 1).
dii.src_spf_vle: FPS Employment, Labour and Social Dialogue — New occupational exposure limit values for lead, its compounds and diisocyanates (03/06/2026, French)
dii.src_spf_ac: FPS Employment, Labour and Social Dialogue — Chemical agents (Codex on well-being at work, Book VI, Title 1, French)
dii.s5_p1: According to the regulation, diisocyanates are used in a wide range of sectors, in particular in foams, sealants and coatings (recital 1). Aromatic diisocyanates (MDI, TDI) are also, together with polyols, the main raw materials of polyurethanes.
dii.s5_l1: Insulation and foams, in particular polyurethane.
dii.s5_p2: The training is aimed in particular at painters, façade workers, waterproofers, joiners and industrial operators who use this type of product, as well as at those who supervise these tasks. Only the label and the safety data sheet tell you whether a specific product is concerned.

dii.a3_sum: Asbestos, crystalline silica, chromium VI, formaldehyde: what the European texts say, compared with diisocyanates.
dii.q1_a: Since 24 August 2023, it is required before any industrial or professional use of a product containing 0.1% or more of diisocyanates by weight, for the people who handle it or who supervise these tasks (Regulation (EU) 2020/1149).
dii.q2: How long is the training valid?
dii.q2_a: The regulation requires it to be renewed at least every five years. It does not create a “European certificate”: it is the employer or self-employed person who documents the successful completion of the training.
dii.q3: Which training level do I need?
dii.q3_a: It depends on your uses: general training applies to everyone; the intermediate level is added in particular for spraying in a ventilated booth or roller and brush application; the advanced level for spraying outside a booth or hot formulations (above 45 °C). See section 03.
dii.q4: What is the fine for non-compliance?
dii.q4_a: Regulation (EU) 2020/1149 does not set any fine amount, and we do not publish unverified figures. For the penalties applicable in Belgium, ask the FPS Employment, Labour and Social Dialogue or your prevention adviser.
dii.q5: What are the duration and the fee?
dii.q5_a: They depend on the level your uses require and are provided on request. Contact the team or call +32 2 318 86 59.
dii.final_p: Tell us your teams' products and uses: the Wisy Safety team will point you to the right training level.
dii.a1_lead: Highly reactive and found in many construction and industrial products, diisocyanates are also powerful sensitisers. What you need to know, according to the official texts.
dii.a1_h1_p: The REACH Regulation uses this name for compounds with the formula O=C=N–R–N=C=O, where R is an aliphatic or aromatic hydrocarbon unit of unspecified length (Annex XVII, entry 74). In other words: two isocyanate groups linked by a carbon chain.
dii.a1_h2_p: The European Chemicals Agency (ECHA) groups 14 substances under the heading “Diisocyanates”. They include:
dii.a1_h2_p2: MDI and TDI are aromatic diisocyanates: together with polyols, they are the main raw materials of polyurethanes, from rigid insulation foams to the flexible foams of mattresses. HDI and IPDI are aliphatic diisocyanates, processed in particular into hardeners for high-quality coatings and adhesives for industrial and professional use.
dii.a1_h3_p: According to Regulation (EU) 2020/1149, diisocyanates are used as chemical building blocks in a wide range of sectors and applications, in particular in foams, sealants and coatings.
dii.a1_h4_l1: Their harmonised classification places them among respiratory sensitisers, category 1, and skin sensitisers, category 1 (CLP Regulation).
dii.a1_h4_l2: Respiratory sensitisation, caused by exposure through the skin and by inhalation, leads to occupational asthma, recognised as a major occupational health problem in the Union.
dii.a1_h4_l3: ECHA's experts also considered that the restriction would reduce cases of dermatitis linked to diisocyanates.
dii.a1_h4_l4: No threshold is known to date for the sensitising effect of diisocyanates.
dii.a1_key: The hazard does not come only from the air you breathe: skin contact matters too. That is why the required training covers dermal and inhalation exposure, protective equipment and ventilation.

dii.a2_lead: Adopted in 2020, applied since 2023: the timeline, the people covered, what the employer must do, the three training levels — and what the text does not say.
dii.a2_l1: 3 August 2020 — adoption of the regulation by the Commission, published in the Official Journal on 4 August 2020 (OJ L 252).
dii.a2_l2: 24 February 2022 — suppliers pass on information about the training requirement and place the prescribed statement on the packaging.
dii.a2_l3: 24 August 2023 — industrial or professional use of a product with 0.1% or more of diisocyanates requires prior successful training.
dii.a2_h1_p: The regulation itself entered into force on the twentieth day following its publication (Article 2); the training obligation has applied since 24 August 2023.
dii.a2_h2_p: Any employed or self-employed worker who handles diisocyanates, on their own or in mixtures, for industrial or professional use — or who supervises these tasks (point 3).
dii.a2_h3: What the employer must do, according to the text
dii.a2_h3_l1: Ensure that users have successfully completed the training before use (point 1 b).
dii.a2_h3_l2: Document the successful completion of the training (point 8).
dii.a2_h3_l3: Have it renewed at least every five years (point 8).
dii.a2_h3_l4: Comply with the provisions set by the Member State for this training (point 6).
dii.a2_h3_p: These obligations come on top of those of the Codex on well-being at work: in Belgium, the employer must in particular assess the risks linked to chemical agents present at the workplace and take the necessary preventive measures (Book VI, Title 1).
dii.a2_h4_l1: General, for all uses: chemistry of diisocyanates, toxicity, exposure, limit values, sensitisation, hygiene, protective equipment, ventilation, cleaning, disposal of packaging.
dii.a2_h4_l2: Intermediate, in particular for spraying in a ventilated booth, roller or brush application and open mixtures at ambient temperature.
dii.a2_h4_l3: Advanced, in particular for spraying outside a booth or high-energy spraying and open handling of hot formulations (above 45 °C).
dii.a2_h4_p: For each level, the text provides for certification or documented proof of successful completion, and specifies “including on-line training”.
dii.a2_h5_p: An expert in occupational safety and health with competence acquired through relevant vocational training (point 4). The supplier of the products, for its part, ensures that the recipient receives training material and courses in the official language(s) of the Member State concerned (point 7).
dii.a2_h6_p: The Royal Decree of 25 May 2026 sets, for all diisocyanates, a limit value of 10 µg NCO/m³ over 8 hours and 20 µg NCO/m³ for short-term exposure, lowered to 6 and 12 µg NCO/m³ from 1 January 2029.
dii.a2_h7: What the text does not say
dii.a2_h7_l1: It does not set any fine amount.
dii.a2_h7_l2: It does not create a “European certificate”: it is the employer or self-employed person who documents successful completion.
dii.a2_h7_l3: It does not replace other occupational safety and health rules: the restriction applies without prejudice to them (point 10).
dii.a2_key: Successful training before any use, documented by the employer and renewed at least every five years.
dii.a3_lead: Asbestos, crystalline silica, chromium VI, formaldehyde: what the European texts say, without an invented hazard scale, and what sets diisocyanates apart.
dii.a3_h1_p: Directive 1999/77/EC recalls that asbestos and products containing it can release fibres that cause asbestosis, mesothelioma and lung cancer, and that no threshold level of exposure below which chrysotile asbestos poses no cancer risk has been identified. Considering that an effective way of protecting health is to ban its use, it adapted the European rules on marketing and use; Member States had to comply by 1 January 2005 at the latest.
dii.a3_h2_p: According to Directive (EU) 2017/2398, there is sufficient evidence of the carcinogenicity of respirable crystalline silica dust. Work involving exposure to this dust generated by a work process was added to Annex I of Directive 2004/37/EC (carcinogens), with a limit value of 0.1 mg/m³ for the respirable fraction.
dii.a3_h3_p: The same directive sets a limit value of 0.005 mg/m³ for carcinogenic chromium (VI) compounds, after transitional values applied until 17 January 2025. Chromium trioxide is also on the REACH authorisation list (Annex XIV, entry 16), with a sunset date of 21 September 2017.
dii.a3_h4_p: Directive (EU) 2019/983 states that formaldehyde meets the criteria for classification as a category 1B carcinogen and that it is also a skin sensitiser. It sets a limit value of 0.37 mg/m³ (0.3 ppm) over 8 hours and 0.74 mg/m³ (0.6 ppm) for short-term exposure.
dii.a3_h5_p: Their common harmonised classification concerns respiratory and skin sensitisation (category 1). Hence a specific approach: successful training required before any professional use (Regulation (EU) 2020/1149) and, in Belgium, specific limit values since 2026.
dii.a3_tcap: Comparison of the official reference points cited in this article
dii.a3_r1d: Member States to comply by 1 January 2005 at the latest
dii.a3_r3d: Limit value of 0.005 mg/m³; authorisation for chromium trioxide
dii.a3_r4d: Limit value of 0.37 mg/m³ over 8 hours
dii.a3_r5b: Respiratory and skin sensitisers (category 1), occupational asthma
dii.a3_r5d: Successful training before use; limit value of 10 µg NCO/m³ over 8 hours
dii.a3_advice: Whatever the substance: know its hazards and read the safety data sheet, ventilate, wear suitable protective equipment, replace the product with a less hazardous one where possible, take care of hygiene and cleaning, and involve the prevention adviser in the risk assessment.
dii.a3_note: This table is not exhaustive: it only covers the texts cited in this article and does not replace your company's risk assessment.
